## Sites

apps/octo_pi_coder/lib/octo_pi/coder/compaction/tokens.ex
\`\`\`elixir
defp user_chars(content) when is_binary(content), do: byte_size(content)
defp user_chars(content) when is_list(content), do: ...
defp tool_result_chars(content) when is_binary(content), do: byte_size(content)
defp tool_result_chars(content) when is_list(content), do: ...
\`\`\`

apps/octo_pi_coder/lib/octo_pi/coder/compaction/serialize.ex
\`\`\`elixir
defp user_text(content) when is_binary(content), do: content
defp user_text(content) when is_list(content), do: ...
defp tool_result_text(content) when is_binary(content), do: content
defp tool_result_text(content) when is_list(content), do: ...
\`\`\`

## Change
After opi-5ka.3 (User.t() / ToolResult.t() content is list-only),
the binary-clause heads are dead code in the well-typed world. Drop
them. The list-clause becomes the only definition.

NB: the JSON-shape clauses (\`%{\"role\" => \"user\", \"content\" => content}\`
in tokens.ex L70) operate on serialized session entries that have
NOT been through Message.normalize; those keep their dual-shape
handling because the on-disk format intentionally stores either form.

## Tests
- Existing tokens_test.exs / serialize_test.exs cases that constructed
  \`%User{content: \"hi\"}\` were updated in opi-5ka.3 to use list-shape;
  they continue to pass.
- Add at least one regression case asserting the dropped binary
  clause is unreachable for User/ToolResult inputs (or verify via
  \`mix dialyzer\` that the type narrowing is exact).

## Depends on
opi-5ka.3 (type narrowing is what makes the binary-clauses dead).
title: Drop dual-shape branches in compaction tokens / serialize
